title: Pour a 10 mL dose of syrup into its dosing cup, held level, and put both down
instruction: Pour 10 mL of syrup from the bottle into the dosing cup, holding the cup up and level while you pour. Then set the cup back on the scale and the bottle back where it stood.
context: Almost every parent measures liquid medicine into the dosing cup that comes with it, pouring to a printed line. Many hold the cup up in one hand at eye level, level, and pour with the other, so they can watch the line as the syrup rises; this trial tests that two-handed way (a cup left on the scale and poured into scores at most 0.5). The bottle is already open: the carer has shaken it and taken off its child-resistant cap; the step tested is measuring the dose. The skill is stopping the stream on the line. Syrup is thick and comes out at about 3 mL/s from a 4 fl oz bottle, so the 9 to 11 mL window is about two thirds of a second, and a dose that is too high cannot be poured back. The job ends with the cup set back on the scale that checks the dose and the bottle put back upright, not dripping.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. (1) A 4 fl oz (118 mL) children's liquid-medicine bottle, amber HDPE with a plain white paper label, standing at x 300 mm, y -180 mm: round body 49 mm across and 82 mm tall, a neck 28 mm across up to a lip 105 mm high with a 22 mm opening, 2 mm walls, holding 118 mL of syrup, 170 g in all. It is already open: the carer has shaken it and taken off its child-resistant push-and-turn cap, which is not on the table. The syrup is Simple Syrup NF, a sealed, shelf-stable pharmacy product sold in 16 fl oz bottles (85 g of sucrose per 100 mL, the base of many children's liquid medicines), used as bought at 20 C (+/- 1 C, probe thermometer): 100 mL in a measuring cylinder weighs 131 g (1.31 g/mL, +/- 1 g), about 150 mPa s (thick, like maple syrup). Flow check before each session: with the bottle held at 76 degrees over a measuring cylinder it must pass 2.5 to 3.5 mL/s; slower, check it is at 20 C, then stir in 10 g of water per kg; faster, use a new bottle. The pads of both grippers are covered with thin disposable nitrile finger sleeves and the scale's pan with cling film (tared with it on), all inside a shallow drip tray. (2) A 30 mL (1 fl oz) clear, see-through round polypropylene dosing cup, 40 mm across and 38 mm tall, 2 mm walls and floor (36 mm inside), 8 g, empty, standing at x 300 mm, y 0, with printed mL graduations at 5 to 30 mL: a 2 mm line at 10 mL and lines at 5, 15, 20, 25 and 30 mL. In the model its wall is 24 flat panels drawn clear (not rendered), with its rolled lip drawn pale grey and its base pale clear; its marks are drawn bolder than real print so the cameras resolve them: rings at 10 mL (red, 6 mm, centred 11.8 mm above its base; 9 to 11 mL is its middle third), 20 and 30 mL (near black, 4 mm); printed numerals 10, 20 and 30 (7 mm) beside the lines on the sides facing each arm; near black 1.5 mm ticks at 5, 15 and 25 mL outside, on each arm's side; a thin opaque golden disc in the cup rides at the level of the syrup poured in (hidden in the floor while the cup is empty). (3) A pocket scale's white platform (its pan), 100 x 100 mm and 14 mm high, fixed, centred at x 300 mm, y 0; the cup stands in its middle. Nothing else is on the table. At the 3 mL/s the neck passes, about 2.2 s at full tilt (a tilt of 76 degrees) puts 10 mL in the cup. The bottle can be lifted by its body; its lip must be above the cup's rim and over its opening, within 14 mm of its axis, to land in it.
scoring: Read each control step from the bottle's and the cup's poses and from both grippers. Dose: the syrup in the cup, from the volume that left the bottle over its lip and fell inside the cup's walls (in a real trial, the cup's content on a 0.1 g scale divided by 1.31 g/mL). Spilled: syrup that left the bottle and did not land in the cup, or that was in a cup tipped more than 45 degrees (a real trial: the bottle's weight loss minus the cup's gain). Unread: the time the stream spent falling into the cup while its lowest point was under 20 mm above the pan or it was tilted more than 5 degrees. Placed: the cup on the pan (centre within 15 mm of the pan's centre, base within 3 mm of its top, tilt under 3 degrees), the bottle upright on its mark (centre within 30 mm, base within 3 mm of the table, tilt under 5 degrees), and both grippers' finger zones 30 mm or more from both parts. Score 0, latched, if more than 15 mL ever stood in the cup, the cup was tipped more than 45 degrees, or more than 10 mL was spilled. Otherwise: 1.0 for 9.0 to 11.0 mL with 0.5 mL or less spilled, 0.15 s or less unread and placed; 0.75 for the same dose with any of that not met; but 0.5 at most if more than 0.15 s was unread or more than 3 mL spilled; 0.5 for 8.0 to 12.0 mL; 0.25 for at least 4 mL; 0 below 4 mL. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: 1.0 with both parts moving under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s, held for 1 s. Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: tare the cup, weigh it (9.0 to 11.0 mL is 11.8 to 14.4 g; 8.0 to 12.0 mL is 10.5 to 15.7 g; 4 mL is 5.2 g; 15 mL is 19.7 g); spilled is the bottle's loss minus the cup's gain (0.5 mL is 0.66 g, 3 mL 3.9 g, 10 mL 13.1 g); unread is counted on 30 fps video: the frames in which syrup is falling into the cup while its base is less than 20 mm above the pan (a 20 mm spacer block beside it for scale) or its wall is more than 5 degrees off a printed angle gauge; more than 4 such frames (0.15 s) is too much; placed uses a ruler on the pan, a 3 mm feeler, a 30 mm spacer against each hand and a protractor.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, no liquid: syrup is a volume ledger on the parts' poses. Surface: the plane holding the volume left in the bore; syrup passes the lip's lowest point at g*w*h^3/(3*nu) (150 mPa s, 1.31 g/mL), capped at 3.0 mL/s by the neck (est), falling straight down. No drip tail or splash. Declared rule: a golden disc in the cup is driven to the ledger's level (display only). Cup: 24 flat wall panels drawn clear (not rendered), pale lip and base; marks and numerals bolder than print.
reset_notes: Stand the bottle upright on its mark with 118 mL (155 g) of 20 C syrup in it. Stand the empty cup in the middle of the pan, film on and tared. Wipe the bottle's lip and body. After each trial: wipe spills with a damp cloth, then dry; renew the finger sleeves and the film if tacky or wet; empty the drip tray; rinse in warm water.
